caption:
A good mind is not enough. How you use it is the practice.

Send this to someone who overthinks and wants to think better.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Link in bio.

#innerspeech #descartes #selftalk #thinking #mindset

text: “It is not enough to have a good mind; the main thing is to use it well.”
Being smart is not the same as thinking well.
Plenty of sharp minds spend years going in circles.
Often the circle runs through your inner voice.
*Why can’t I get this right? What if it goes wrong?*
That voice is a tool.
Used well, it plans, questions and encourages.
Used carelessly, it only repeats.
Using it well starts with listening.
What exactly are you saying to yourself, and in what tone?
Try this today:
When you catch a loop, say the next sentence out loud.
Hearing it often changes it.
Then answer it like a fair friend would.
Not with flattery, not with scorn.
With one honest, useful sentence.
What does your inner voice say most often when you are trying to think?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
Learn to use the voice you think with, on purpose.
Hear the voice.
*Use it well.*

header: On what you think you know
caption:
Being certain and being right are not the same thing.

Save this, then test one belief you are sure about.

From "Learn To Think For Yourself." Link in bio.

#thinkforyourself #epictetus #criticalthinking #openmind #mindset

text: “It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.”
The hardest thing to learn is the thing you are sure of.
Certainty feels like knowledge. It is often just a closed door.
Think of an opinion you have never questioned.
Where did it come from? Who handed it to you?
Being sure is comfortable.
It saves you the work of looking again.
Thinking for yourself starts with one humble sentence:
*I might be missing something.*
That sentence is not weakness.
It is how a mind stays open long enough to grow.
Pick one belief this week and test it.
Read the best case against it. Then decide again.
Which belief of yours has never once been tested?
This is the thread behind the book *Learn To Think For Yourself*.
Open the door you closed.
Question what feels certain.
*Keep what survives.*

caption:
You do not need the whole map. You need the next step.

Try it: pick one two-minute step and do it before bed.

From "The 14-Day Clarity Reset." Link in bio.

#clarityreset #laotzu #smallsteps #dailyhabits #mindset

text: “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.”
Big change is rarely stopped by difficulty.
It is stopped by not knowing where to put your foot first.
Clarity does not arrive all at once.
It shows up after you move, not before.
So shrink the first step until it is almost embarrassing.
Two minutes. One page. One honest sentence.
A small step does something a plan cannot.
It turns *someday* into *today*, and today is where you live.
Do not judge the step by its size.
Judge it by whether it was actually taken.
Tomorrow, take another.
The road gets clearer from the middle.
What is the smallest step you could take in the next ten minutes?
This is the thread behind the book *The 14-Day Clarity Reset*.
One small step a day, for fourteen days.
Start small.
*Start today.*

caption:
A harsh thought is often a tired feeling in disguise.

Save this for the next time your inner voice gets loud.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Link in bio.

#innerspeech #nietzsche #selftalk #emotionalawareness #mindset

text: “Our thoughts are the shadows of our feelings, always darker, emptier and simpler.”
A thought can feel like a fact.
But often it is a feeling wearing words.
When you are tired, the inner voice turns harsh.
*I always fail. Nothing works.* Always. Nothing. Those are shadow words.
Shadows are simpler than the things that cast them.
They have no detail, no color, no exceptions.
So when a thought lands hard, ask:
*What am I feeling underneath this sentence?*
Name it: tired, afraid, hurt, rushed.
Often the thought softens once the feeling is seen.
Then rewrite the line with the detail put back in.
*I failed at this one thing today, and I am tired.*
What feeling is standing behind the harshest thing you said to yourself today?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
Learn to read your own shadows.
Hear the words.
*Find the feeling.*
